metadata.title: Dabrafenib Monotherapy
metadata.indication: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed BRAF V600 mutation.
metadata.partial_assessment_note: Any independently actionable entered value is assessed; omitted domains remain unassessed and do not block a partial result.
metadata.partial_assessment_policy: Each entered value is assessed independently. Omitted domains remain unassessed and are never assumed normal.

catalogue_reconciliation.scope_note: The NCCP states that its website list is not comprehensive. This reconciliation does not assert that every possible national regimen is published online.

encoding_maturity.label: Current source reconciled; independent clinical/pharmacy review pending
encoding_maturity.scope_note: NCCP tables individually reconciled; proposed candidate awaits validation and independent clinical/pharmacy approval.

supplemental_source_documents.section: Current EMA product information supplement, component-specific

clinical_governance.prescriptive_authority: Treatment plan must be initiated by a Consultant Medical Oncologist or the specialist authority specified in the current NCCP source.
clinical_governance.dose_modification_note: All modifications require consultant/pharmacy review. Component-specific advice and dose levels are reference text, never an automatically calculated prescription. Missing values remain unassessed.
clinical_governance.disclaimer: Decision-support encoding derived from NCCP 00237 Version 6. It does not replace the current official regimen, prescribing review, pharmacy verification or independent clinical judgement.

source_conflicts.resolution: NCCP 00237 v6 pp2/4 specifies ≥38.5°C, while current EMA Tafinlar p4 §4.2/p9 §4.4 explicitly specifies ≥38°C for monotherapy. Preserve the lower SmPC safety hold and label the discrepancy; require clinician/pharmacy resolution.

removed_unsupported_generic_rules: Legacy shared whole-regimen QT/LVEF/CK/ILD/haemorrhage shortcuts were replaced only where a source-specific pathway exists. Named symptoms without source dose criteria prompt assessment, not invented thresholds.

indications.description: Adult patients with unresectable or metastatic melanoma with a confirmed BRAF V600 mutation.

treatment.schedule_summary: Dabrafenib 150 mg twice daily continuously; use a 28-day assessment-cycle convention. Continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity.
treatment.cycle_convention_note: 28 days is an assessment convention; treatment is continuous without planned breaks.

administration.note: About 12 hours apart, at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after food; continuous treatment.

action.message: Validated BRAF V600 mutation is required; do not use the regimen for wild-type melanoma.

action.message: Reconcile source-specific blood, ECG, skin and other surveillance before treatment.

action.message: Confirm the current dose, prior reductions, episode history and component attribution; do not calculate an automatic restart dose.

action.message: Do not restart the interrupted other-toxicity pathway until grade 0–1 recovery; permanent-stop history remains separately assessed.

rules.explanation: Do not restart the interrupted other-toxicity pathway until grade 0–1 recovery; permanent-stop history remains separately assessed.

action.message: Arrange prompt ophthalmic assessment and establish the diagnosis; a symptom alone does not mandate an invented universal whole-regimen interruption.

rules.explanation: Arrange prompt ophthalmic assessment and establish the diagnosis; a symptom alone does not mandate an invented universal whole-regimen interruption.

action.message: Arrange dermatology assessment and pathology for a new lesion; do not treat it as a proven diagnosis.

rules.explanation: Arrange dermatology assessment and pathology for a new lesion; do not treat it as a proven diagnosis.

action.message: Manage cutaneous SCC with dermatological excision/review. This finding alone does not require dose reduction; other toxicities remain separately assessed.

rules.explanation: Manage cutaneous SCC with dermatological excision/review. This finding alone does not require dose reduction; other toxicities remain separately assessed.

action.message: No renal dose adjustment is needed at CrCl ≥30 mL/min; this renal finding is not clearance of other domains.

rules.explanation: No renal dose adjustment is needed at CrCl ≥30 mL/min; this renal finding is not clearance of other domains.

action.message: The source expects no renal dose adjustment at CrCl <30 mL/min. Individual clinical review remains necessary; do not invent a renal contraindication or reduction.

rules.explanation: The source expects no renal dose adjustment at CrCl <30 mL/min. Individual clinical review remains necessary; do not invent a renal contraindication or reduction.

action.message: The source expects no dose adjustment on haemodialysis; confirm the individual plan with oncology pharmacy.

rules.explanation: The source expects no dose adjustment on haemodialysis; confirm the individual plan with oncology pharmacy.

action.message: No dose adjustment is needed for mild hepatic impairment.

rules.explanation: No dose adjustment is needed for mild hepatic impairment.

action.message: For moderate/severe hepatic impairment, 50% of the original dabrafenib dose MAY be considered. This is a consultant choice, not an automatic calculated dose.

rules.explanation: For moderate/severe hepatic impairment, 50% of the original dabrafenib dose MAY be considered. This is a consultant choice, not an automatic calculated dose.

action.message: Previous treatment failure with a BRAF inhibitor is an NCCP exclusion; intolerance is a different history.

rules.explanation: Previous treatment failure with a BRAF inhibitor is an NCCP exclusion; intolerance is a different history.

action.message: Uncontrolled hypertension is an NCCP exclusion; correct and review before treatment.

rules.explanation: Uncontrolled hypertension is an NCCP exclusion; correct and review before treatment.

action.message: Uncontrolled electrolyte abnormalities are an NCCP exclusion; correct and review before treatment.

rules.explanation: Uncontrolled electrolyte abnormalities are an NCCP exclusion; correct and review before treatment.

action.message: Sequential BRAF inhibitor treatment may be considered after intolerance; confirm that this was not treatment failure.

rules.explanation: Sequential BRAF inhibitor treatment may be considered after intolerance; confirm that this was not treatment failure.

action.message: NCCP dabrafenib monotherapy specifies interruption at ≥38.5°C; current EMA Tafinlar specifies ≥38°C for monotherapy. At this temperature both sources require interruption and assessment for infection; follow the reconciled treating-team pyrexia plan.

rules.explanation: NCCP dabrafenib monotherapy specifies interruption at ≥38.5°C; current EMA Tafinlar specifies ≥38°C for monotherapy. At this temperature both sources require interruption and assessment for infection; follow the reconciled treating-team pyrexia plan.

action.message: SOURCE DISCREPANCY: current EMA Tafinlar §4.2/4.4 instructs interruption of MONOTHERAPY at ≥38°C; NCCP 00237 v6 specifies ≥38.5°C. At 38–38.49°C keep dabrafenib withheld, assess infection and obtain treating-team/pharmacy reconciliation. Do not treat this interval as cleared.

rules.explanation: SOURCE DISCREPANCY: current EMA Tafinlar §4.2/4.4 instructs interruption of MONOTHERAPY at ≥38°C; NCCP 00237 v6 specifies ≥38.5°C. At 38–38.49°C keep dabrafenib withheld, assess infection and obtain treating-team/pharmacy reconciliation. Do not treat this interval as cleared.

action.message: Current EMA permits interruption at the first symptom of recurrent pyrexia, before a measured fever threshold; assess infection and obtain the agreed pyrexia plan.

rules.explanation: Current EMA permits interruption at the first symptom of recurrent pyrexia, before a measured fever threshold; assess infection and obtain the agreed pyrexia plan.

action.message: Current EMA requires at least 24 hours symptom-free before restarting. Reported resolution alone is insufficient; assess infection and recurrence/severe features.

rules.explanation: Current EMA requires at least 24 hours symptom-free before restarting. Reported resolution alone is insufficient; assess infection and recurrence/severe features.

action.message: Record at least 24 hours symptom-free before considering restart under current EMA product information; do not assume the elapsed time.

rules.explanation: Record at least 24 hours symptom-free before considering restart under current EMA product information; do not assume the elapsed time.

action.message: Current EMA recommends one-dose-level reduction for recurrent and/or severe pyrexia after at least 24 hours symptom-free. The NCCP monotherapy document is less detailed; follow the reconciled consultant/pharmacy plan.

rules.explanation: Current EMA recommends one-dose-level reduction for recurrent and/or severe pyrexia after at least 24 hours symptom-free. The NCCP monotherapy document is less detailed; follow the reconciled consultant/pharmacy plan.

action.message: Do not restart dabrafenib while fever persists; assess infection and the severity of the episode.

rules.explanation: Do not restart dabrafenib while fever persists; assess infection and the severity of the episode.

action.message: After fever resolves, consultant may restart with appropriate prescribed prophylaxis. Severe associated signs/symptoms require a reduced restart dose. Do not auto-prescribe NSAIDs/paracetamol or infer infection excluded.

rules.explanation: After fever resolves, consultant may restart with appropriate prescribed prophylaxis. Severe associated signs/symptoms require a reduced restart dose. Do not auto-prescribe NSAIDs/paracetamol or infer infection excluded.

action.message: Once severe febrile events resolve, restart at a reduced dabrafenib dose only when clinically appropriate and after review.

rules.explanation: Once severe febrile events resolve, restart at a reduced dabrafenib dose only when clinically appropriate and after review.

action.message: No dabrafenib reduction is recommended while effective local therapy controls uveitis; continue ophthalmic review.

rules.explanation: No dabrafenib reduction is recommended while effective local therapy controls uveitis; continue ophthalmic review.

action.message: Uveitis not responding to local therapy: withhold until ocular inflammation resolves, then consultant may restart one dose level lower.

rules.explanation: Uveitis not responding to local therapy: withhold until ocular inflammation resolves, then consultant may restart one dose level lower.

action.message: Establish local ocular response; controlled uveitis does not automatically require a hold or reduction.

rules.explanation: Establish local ocular response; controlled uveitis does not automatically require a hold or reduction.

action.message: After an interruption for uncontrolled uveitis, wait for resolution of ocular inflammation before considering the reduced restart.

rules.explanation: After an interruption for uncontrolled uveitis, wait for resolution of ocular inflammation before considering the reduced restart.

action.message: Carefully assess benefit and risk with prior/concurrent RAS-mutated non-cutaneous cancer.

rules.explanation: Carefully assess benefit and risk with prior/concurrent RAS-mutated non-cutaneous cancer.

action.message: Source cautions include congenital long QT, high cumulative anthracycline exposure, QT-prolonging medicines and electrolyte disturbances; no automatic QTc>500 permanent-stop algorithm is specified for dabrafenib monotherapy.

rules.explanation: Source cautions include congenital long QT, high cumulative anthracycline exposure, QT-prolonging medicines and electrolyte disturbances; no automatic QTc>500 permanent-stop algorithm is specified for dabrafenib monotherapy.

action.message: Review a rising creatinine; interruption may be needed as clinically appropriate.

rules.explanation: Review a rising creatinine; interruption may be needed as clinically appropriate.

action.message: Promptly investigate unexplained abdominal pain, including amylase/lipase; assess pancreatitis and monitor closely on any restart.

rules.explanation: Promptly investigate unexplained abdominal pain, including amylase/lipase; assess pancreatitis and monitor closely on any restart.

action.message: Dabrafenib has not been studied at creatinine >1.5×ULN; use caution. This is not a numerical dose-reduction or absolute contraindication rule.

rules.explanation: Dabrafenib has not been studied at creatinine >1.5×ULN; use caution. This is not a numerical dose-reduction or absolute contraindication rule.

action.message: New primary melanomas were managed by excision without treatment modification in the source; arrange dermatology management and continued surveillance.

rules.explanation: New primary melanomas were managed by excision without treatment modification in the source; arrange dermatology management and continued surveillance.

action.message: Other intolerable grade 2 or grade 3 toxicity: interrupt until grade 0–1, then reduce one level. Reference steps are 150→100→75→50 mg twice daily; no reduction below 50 mg twice daily is recommended.

rules.explanation: Other intolerable grade 2 or grade 3 toxicity: interrupt until grade 0–1, then reduce one level. Reference steps are 150→100→75→50 mg twice daily; no reduction below 50 mg twice daily is recommended.

action.message: Grade 4: consultant chooses permanent discontinuation OR interruption until grade 0–1 and one-level reduction on restart. This source does not impose automatic permanent cessation solely for recurrence; review the full history.

rules.explanation: Grade 4: consultant chooses permanent discontinuation OR interruption until grade 0–1 and one-level reduction on restart. This source does not impose automatic permanent cessation solely for recurrence; review the full history.

action.message: Further reduction below 50 mg twice daily is not recommended. Obtain a consultant decision rather than invent a lower dose.

rules.explanation: Further reduction below 50 mg twice daily is not recommended. Obtain a consultant decision rather than invent a lower dose.

action.message: Dabrafenib dose must not exceed 150 mg twice daily. Re-escalation after toxicity is a consultant option only when adverse reactions are effectively controlled.

rules.explanation: Dabrafenib dose must not exceed 150 mg twice daily. Re-escalation after toxicity is a consultant option only when adverse reactions are effectively controlled.

action.message: Dose adjustment below 50 mg twice daily is not recommended. Reconcile the source and prescribing plan.

rules.explanation: Dose adjustment below 50 mg twice daily is not recommended. Reconcile the source and prescribing plan.

eligibility: Adult unresectable/metastatic melanoma with validated BRAF V600 mutation
exclusions: Known hypersensitivity to a regimen component
Pregnancy or breastfeeding where prohibited by the current source
Regimen-specific exclusions encoded in the assessment

supportive_care.mapping_basis: Highest emetogenic active component and current NCCP classification.
supportive_care.supportive_medications_label: NCCP antiemetic guidance for oral SACT
supportive_care.source_audit_note: Vemurafenib monotherapy: minimal emetogenic potential; dabrafenib and cobimetinib/vemurafenib: minimal-to-low. Premedication not usually required; antiemetics per local policy. No default prophylactic medicines prescribed.

baseline: FBC, renal and liver profile; ECG
Head/neck examination including oral mucosa and lymph nodes; chest/abdomen CT for secondary-malignancy assessment
Anal examination and pelvic examination for women as advised by source/clinical plan
during: FBC, renal and liver profile monthly; ECG as clinically indicated
Skin examination monthly; head/neck examination every three months
Review creatinine, unexplained abdominal pain and visual symptoms
Secondary-malignancy surveillance may include chest/abdomen CT every six months; this is distinct from response imaging
after: Skin and non-cutaneous secondary-malignancy surveillance up to six months after cessation or until another antineoplastic therapy
Anal/pelvic examinations at treatment end or as clinically indicated
Alternative effective contraception during therapy and for two weeks after, because hormonal methods may be less effective
monitoring.disease_monitoring: Consultant treatment plan; secondary-malignancy surveillance is not a universal tumour-response imaging schedule.
